subject: KV-cache & ephemeral-log retention exception for Private deployment
messages:
From: John Ellis <john.ellis@medsol.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@medsol.com
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: KV-cache & ephemeral-log retention in private deployment

Markus,

Thanks for taking this. We are preparing our SIG/CAIQ pack for an upcoming audit and have a customer-specific retention requirement to discuss for the Private deployment you provisioned in our VPC. MedSol's data governance requires that certain inference-level ephemeral artifacts (we'll call them 'kv-cache traces' for lack of a better name) be retained no longer than 14 days, whereas your standard policy for session and diagnostic logs is 30 days.

We understand the operational tradeoffs but need a formal exception path + evidence for the auditor. Specifically, we need:
- A brief statement of whether Redwood can support a tenant-scoped TTL of 14 days for kv-cache traces in Private deployments (noting any platform limitations).
- The controls that ensure the 14-day TTL is enforced (automated deletion, immutable retention windows, access controls).
- How emergency legal hold/forensics is handled if MedSol issues a preservation notice (we need the process + expected timelines).
- Example artifacts: a signed attestation or a small evidence pack that the auditor can consume (log retention policy text, samples of the deletion job logs, encryption-at-rest confirmation).

Can you also confirm whether acceptance of this exception requires a contract amendment or PO line item? Procurement is copied. I'm happy to schedule a short call if it's easier.

Attachment: MedSol_SAR_requirements.pdf

Regards,
John Ellis
Head of Compliance
MedSol Health

Reply requested: yes.

Subject: Re: KV-cache & ephemeral-log retention in private deployment

John — thanks for the clear ask and the SAR doc. Short answer: we can support a tenant-scoped reduction to a 14-day TTL for the inference-layer ephemeral artifacts in Private (VPC) installs, with a couple of caveats and compensating controls. Outline below and happy to jump on a 20-min call to align.

What we can offer (high level):
- Tenant-scoped TTL override: We can configure the private control plane to apply a 14-day retention policy for the kv-cache artifacts for your tenant only. This will be applied at the storage lifecycle layer and at the runtime eviction layer.
- Enforcement: deletion jobs run daily; objects are irreversibly removed after the TTL expires (we maintain deletion logs). Retention is implemented using object metadata + scheduled garbage collection.
- Compensating controls: data encrypted at rest (KMS) and role-based access to the retention management service; we can scope audit roles to only Redwood SOC/forensics with explicit Just-In-Time access requests documented.
- Legal hold: if MedSol issues a preservation notice, we will suspend deletion for the affected tenant and immediately snapshot the relevant artifacts into a temporarily held escrow bucket (encrypted, access-limited). This is a manual action that requires an authorized contact from MedSol + legal review; we will provide timestamps of when the hold was enacted.

What we need from MedSol:
- An authorized request (email from a Legal/Compliance owner) to enable the 14-day policy and to outline the approved authorized individuals for legal holds.
- Acceptance that enabling the exception will be recorded as a customer-specific configuration; if your procurement requires contract language we can add a short addendum.

Next steps / proposed deliverables from Redwood (we'll attach these):
1) A short one-page attestation describing the tenant-scoped 14-day TTL and enforcement mechanism.
2) Sample deletion-job logs (redacted) showing a scheduled GC run and object deletions.
3) A brief runbook describing the legal-hold workflow and expected timelines.

I'll open an internal evidence bundle (kvcache-retention-exception-evidence.zip) and loop in Hannah from Security to validate technical details. Neha — please confirm commercial/contract routing if procurement needs an addendum.

Happy to take this to a quick call; I'm available 1–3pm PT today or tomorrow.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Markus / team — forwarding my quick tech notes so we capture expectations.

On Thu, Apr 29, 2028 at 10:45 AM markus_klein@redwood.com wrote:
> John — thanks for the clear ask...

My notes (high level):
- Definition: we need to align on what "kv-cache traces" actually include (raw KV blobs, request/response prefixes, debug traces). The retention mechanism and legal-hold behavior differ slightly depending on which of the above are in scope. Please confirm the object prefixes or example keys if possible.
- Implementation: we will use a two-tier cleanup: (1) runtime eviction (fast) to drop in-memory entries and (2) scheduled GC on object store to delete persisted artifacts after 14 days. The runtime eviction is immediate and per-request, but only the object-store deletions are auditable.
- Evidence artifacts: we can provide GC job logs, object metadata schema, and a sample KMS key ARN statement. We cannot produce raw customer data as part of an evidence pack — only metadata and deletion confirmations.
- Legal hold process: we will require a signed preservation request template (we will provide) and a named MedSol contact authorized to request holds. Once received, we will: (a) pause GC for the affected tenant, (b) snapshot current objects to an escrow bucket, (c) provide MD5 checksums and timestamps, (d) restrict access until release. Target: hold action within 24 hours of a valid request, but this may vary by time zone and approvals.

Open questions for John/MedSol:
1) Can you enumerate which of the kv-cache artifacts must be retained 14 days vs excluded entirely? If there are PII elements we may need additional redaction tooling.
2) Is MedSol comfortable with an operational window for legal-hold enactment of up to 24 hours? We will include SLA language if you need stricter commitments (procurement/legal).

I can draft the short attestation and the runbook; Markus, can you confirm whether we need a formal addendum template for procurement?

-Hannah
Head of Security Assurance
Redwood Inference

- Scope: "kv-cache traces" = persisted inference cache objects and debug traces that are stored in the private object store under prefix /tenants/medsol/kvcache/*. Request/response transcripts that are stored elsewhere are out of scope.
- Evidence: the auditor (Laura Chen) asked for a single-page attestation + one example GC job log (redacted) + the legal-hold runbook. The attestation should state the tenant-scoped 14-day TTL, deletion automation, and that deletion logs are retained for at least 90 days for audit purposes.
- Contracting: procurement notes that a short addendum acknowledging the tenant-scoped configuration and the legal-hold workflow will suffice. Please route a draft addendum to procurement@medsol.com.

Action items we will take: MedSol will send a single authorized email from Legal (cc: procurement) confirming the authorized legal-hold contacts within 48 hours.

If you can provide the attestation and the runbook by end of next week (May 7), we can close the SIG artifact set.
